## Read first
- docs/enhanced-architecture-diagrams.md, the "BUILD STATUS" section (§S1–S6).
  It is the build truth and supersedes the 18 design diagrams wherever they
  conflict. §S2 and §S3 have been corrected against the probe evidence and are
  authoritative. conf/generated/capabilities.ASHWINRAVI004.yml overrides any
  prose, including them.
- sql/README.md — the SQL template contract (the sql_context variable list).
- conf/generation.yml — every Phase 2 parameter.

Environment: .venv (Python 3.12), project installed editable. Connection
ASHWINRAVI004 (ZC14131, STANDARD edition, trial, AWS_AP_SOUTHEAST_7) via
SNOWFLAKE_JWT, key path in .env. Verify with:
  .\.venv\Scripts\riskcopilot.exe --profile dev doctor

## Where things stand
Phase 0 (three-tier config, CLI, doctor, idempotent SQL deployer, capability
gating) and Phase 1 (28 tables across 7 schemas) are done and deployed.
125 unit tests pass; mypy --strict and ruff clean; all SQL templates render for
both profiles; `deploy --stage bootstrap` idempotent across consecutive runs.
capabilities.py makes doctor read the evidence file and auto-disable unavailable
features (13/27 enabled, 0 failures).

## Capability reality — measured, not assumed
Evidence: conf/generated/capabilities.ASHWINRAVI004.yml (98 probes, 30
available). doctor reads it and auto-disables what is absent. Full map in §S2.

Three earlier assumptions were WRONG; do not reintroduce them:
1. "All Cortex AI unavailable" — false. Cortex Analyst NL→SQL works (REST,
   HTTP 200, real SQL, served by claude-sonnet-4-6), as do AI_AGG and
   AI_SUMMARIZE_AGG. Text-to-SQL eval (Suite 2) is scorable NOW.
2. "SNOWFLAKE.ML requires Enterprise" — false. Anomaly detection, Forecast,
   Model Registry and Feature Store all work on Standard trial.
3. "Search/Agent/Analyst blocked because AI_COMPLETE is" — unsound inference.
   They are gated independently. Never generalise gating from one probe.

The entire pipeline critical path works and is probe-confirmed: dynamic tables
(with refresh), STREAM ON DYNAMIC TABLE, tasks (warehouse + serverless),
EXECUTE TASK, MERGE with unique constraint, recursive CTE, Python stored
procedures (no Anaconda blocker), SQL procedures, Streamlit, network rules.

Net effect: narrative generation is the ONLY genuinely blocked piece of the
copilot. Out of scope on this account: per-row Cortex inference (AI_COMPLETE
399258, four independent paths), agent invocation (399504 — the object still
deploys), Cortex Search (EMBED_TEXT blocked), External Access Integration
(509009, kills the Jira/Slack/MCP loop), and the Enterprise governance features
(row access policies, masking, DMFs, Time Travel > 1 day, all 000002).
ML.CLASSIFICATION and TOP_INSIGHTS are REGIONAL, not trial — converting will
not fix those.

Treat two findings as unsettled: the 403/003001 → trial classification is an
inference (Snowflake never says "trial"), and whether ENABLE_AI_COST_ESTIMATE is
switchable on this account is unknown.

## Fix these first — both contradicted by evidence, both still live
1. conf/ml.yml: `preconditions.require_edition: [ENTERPRISE, BUSINESS_CRITICAL]`
   is wrong and currently disables a WORKING feature. Anomaly detection,
   Forecast, Model Registry and Feature Store all work here. Re-enable
   tier1.velocity_anomaly, and move CLASSIFICATION/TOP_INSIGHTS to future_scope
   with "not served in this region" as the reason.
2. conf/profiles/demo.yml: retention.landing_days / evidence_days are 14.
   Standard caps Time Travel at 1 day, so a demo-profile deploy WILL fail.
   Cap it, or better, have config.py clamp retention using the capabilities
   evidence.

## Task: Phase 2 — data synthesis, thin vertical slice
Per §S6, build one slice end-to-end before broadening. Create under
src/risk_copilot/generation/:

  patterns.py       parse HI-Small_Patterns.txt -> attempts + seed accounts
  graph.py          subgraph sampling (BFS 2 hops from laundering seeds) + ID maps
  reskin.py         per-currency FX -> INR, channel remap, pair -> two signed legs
  entities.py       Faker enrichment of PRESERVED keys, correlated income, devices
  relationships.py  attribute edges (shared phone/device, beneficial owner)
  inject.py         structuring cohort first; other cohorts after
  labels.py         leg-level labels with match_confidence
  eval_grain.py     party-month evaluation truth
  validate.py       the realism gates
  demo_entity.py    select and pin the hero party

Then wire `riskcopilot generate` (currently a stub in cli.py), with unit tests
per module.

All parameters come from conf/generation.yml — seeds, subgraph targets, FX rates,
channel map, income correlation, device co-location, injection cohorts,
validation gates, demo-entity criteria. Nothing is invented in code.

For the first slice, only structuring injection is needed. Skip L3 narratives
(blocked) and the other cohorts until the slice runs end to end.

## Invariants — do not break these
- No hardcoded values. Topology from conf/ via Settings.sql_context(); business
  thresholds from GOVERNANCE.POLICY_CLAUSE at runtime, never literals in code or
  SQL. The deployer REJECTS any .sql containing a literal object name.
- ids.py is the referential backbone. AMLworld keys are authoritative; surrogate
  ids derive deterministically from them. Never mint independent party ids —
  that was the worst defect in the original design (§S5 gap 2).
- GROUND_TRUTH is isolated. No label may reach RAW_TRANSACTIONS, CURATED or the
  semantic view. The service role has no USAGE on that schema.
- Reproducible generation: same seed -> byte-identical output. Draw per-entity
  attributes via derived_rng(entity_id, seed, namespace), never from a single
  global stream, so output does not depend on iteration order.
- Validation gates with fail_build: true must actually fail the build.
- Every SQL statement idempotent. One string literal per line — Snowflake does
  not concatenate adjacent literals (this caused 60 syntax errors once already).
- ML may rank and flag for review; it may never supply a number that appears in
  an artifact (RULE_DEFINITION.admissible_as_primary_evidence).
- Capability gating reads conf/generated/capabilities.*.yml. Never hardcode a
  feature as unavailable, and never infer one gate from another.
- Tool logic lives in Snowflake stored procedures, never in Python. That is the
  only reason migration to a Cortex Agent is a config change rather than a
  rewrite. If you find yourself writing tool logic in Python, stop.
- Reviewer is a stored procedure, NOT an agent mode. Determinism is its entire
  value. Sentinel is a SQL view plus one AI_AGG call. Only Investigator and
  Drafter are agent modes. See §S3 "Correction to Diagram 7".

1|# ===========================================================================
     2|# generation.yml -- synthetic data generation parameters
     3|# ===========================================================================
     4|# Every number that shapes the dataset lives here. Changing the seed and
     5|# re-running must reproduce a byte-identical dataset: that is what makes the
     6|# evaluation numbers defensible.
     7|# ===========================================================================
     8|
     9|seed: 20260922        # master seed; every sub-generator derives from it
    10|
    11|# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    12|# GAP-02 -- subgraph sampling.
    13|# AMLworld ships 518,581 accounts / ~700K entities. We do NOT generate parties
    14|# independently and hope they join: we sample a CONNECTED subgraph of the real
    15|# transaction graph and then enrich the preserved keys. Seeding from the
    16|# laundering attempts guarantees the illicit typologies survive sampling.
    17|# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    18|subgraph:
    19|  seed_source: laundering_patterns   # accounts named in HI-Small_Patterns.txt
    20|  expansion_hops: 2                  # BFS hops along the transaction graph
    21|  target_parties: 5000
    22|  target_accounts: 10000
    23|  max_transactions: 400000
    24|  # A leg is kept only if BOTH sides resolve to a sampled account. Guarantees
    25|  # referential integrity of counterparty_account_id by construction.
    26|  require_both_legs_resolvable: true
    27|  # Cap on how much of one high-degree hub's neighbourhood is pulled in, so a
    28|  # single hub cannot dominate the sample.
    29|  max_neighbours_per_account: 40
    30|
    31|# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    32|# GAP-06 -- FX. A blanket x83 is wrong across 14 currencies. Rates are
    33|# indicative period rates for the AMLworld window (2022 H2), applied per
    34|# source currency.
    35|# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    36|fx:
    37|  base_currency: INR
    38|  rates_to_inr:
    39|    "US Dollar": 82.50
    40|    "Euro": 86.20
    41|    "UK Pound": 99.40
    42|    "Yen": 0.58
    43|    "Yuan": 11.50
    44|    "Rupee": 1.00
    45|    "Australian Dollar": 54.80
    46|    "Canadian Dollar": 60.90
    47|    "Swiss Franc": 87.60
    48|    "Mexican Peso": 4.15
    49|    "Ruble": 1.05
    50|    "Saudi Riyal": 22.00
    51|    "Shekel": 24.10
    52|    "Brazil Real": 15.60
    53|  # Share of legs deliberately retained in foreign currency so cross-border
    54|  # signals have something to bite on.
    55|  retain_foreign_pct: 5.0
    56|  rounding_decimals: 2
    57|
    58|# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    59|# Channel remapping: AMLworld payment formats -> Indian rails.
    60|# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    61|channel_map:
    62|  ACH: NEFT
    63|  Wire: RTGS
    64|  Cheque: CHEQUE
    65|  Cash: CASH
    66|  "Credit Card": UPI
    67|  Reinvestment: IMPS
    68|channel_default: NEFT
    69|
    70|# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    71|# GAP-03 -- pair-to-leg conversion.
    72|# One AMLworld pair row becomes two rows sharing a txn_pair_id: a signed
    73|# negative debit on the sender and a signed positive credit on the receiver.
    74|# The pair-level shape used by graph queries is exposed as V_TRANSACTION_PAIRS.
    75|# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    76|legs:
    77|  debit_sign: -1
    78|  credit_sign: 1
    79|  # AMLworld carries distinct paid/received amounts for FX pairs; each leg
    80|  # keeps its own side's amount so money conservation holds per currency.
    81|  use_side_specific_amounts: true
    82|
    83|# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    84|# L1 -- entity enrichment. These attributes DRESS the preserved AMLworld keys.
    85|# Attributes are derived from hash(entity_id), so a rerun is idempotent and a
    86|# party's identity is stable even if the sample changes size.
    87|# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    88|entities:
    89|  faker_locale: hi_IN
    90|  party_type_from_entity_name:
    91|    Corporation: LEGAL_PERSON
    92|    Partnership: LEGAL_PERSON
    93|    "Sole Proprietorship": LEGAL_PERSON
    94|    Company: LEGAL_PERSON
    95|    Individual: INDIVIDUAL
    96|  party_type_default: INDIVIDUAL
    97|
    98|  # Must match roles.branch_analysts keys in conf/base.yml. Drives RLS.
    99|  branch_regions:
   100|    - { code: MUMBAI, weight: 0.40 }
   101|    - { code: DELHI,  weight: 0.35 }
   102|    - { code: PUNE,   weight: 0.25 }   # no analyst role -> proves RLS excludes
   103|
   104|  account_types:
   105|    - { code: SAVINGS,     weight: 0.45 }
   106|    - { code: CURRENT,     weight: 0.25 }
   107|    - { code: LOAN,        weight: 0.12 }
   108|    - { code: CREDIT_CARD, weight: 0.10 }
   109|    - { code: FD,          weight: 0.08 }
   110|
   111|  pep_pct: 1.5
   112|  risk_rating_distribution:
   113|    LOW: 0.70
   114|    MEDIUM: 0.22
   115|    HIGH: 0.08
   116|  kyc_status_distribution:
   117|    VERIFIED: 0.88
   118|    PENDING_REVIEW: 0.09
   119|    EXPIRED: 0.03
   120|
   121|  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
   122|  # GAP-04 -- declared income MUST correlate with observed legitimate inflow,
   123|  # or INCOME_ACTIVITY_MISMATCH fires on everybody or nobody. Income is
   124|  # derived from each party's own legit 12-month inflow, divided by a
   125|  # plausible coverage ratio, with lognormal noise. The illicit cohort then
   126|  # deliberately under-declares, which is what the rule is supposed to find.
   127|  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
   128|  income:
   129|    derive_from: legit_inflow_12m
   130|    coverage_ratio_mean: 1.15        # declared ~= annual legit inflow / 1.15
   131|    coverage_ratio_sigma: 0.28
   132|    noise_lognormal_sigma: 0.22
   133|    floor_inr: 180000
   134|    ceiling_inr: 250000000
   135|    round_to_inr: 10000
   136|    illicit_cohort_under_declare_factor: 0.35   # declare ~35% of true capacity
   137|
   138|  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
   139|  # GAP-05 -- shared device fingerprints must be co-located with existing fund
   140|  # flows, because SHARED_DEVICE_CLUSTER requires shared device AND flow
   141|  # between the accounts. Random assignment yields zero detections.
   142|  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
   143|  device:
   144|    shared_fingerprint_pct: 8.0
   145|    # Fraction of shared-device clusters placed on account groups that already
   146|    # transact with each other. The remainder are decoys (shared device, no
   147|    # flow) that the rule must correctly NOT fire on -- these are the
   148|    # false-positive control.
   149|    colocate_with_fund_flow_pct: 70.0
   150|    cluster_size_min: 3
   151|    cluster_size_max: 5
   152|
   153|  relationships:
   154|    shared_phone_pct: 4.0
   155|    beneficial_owner_pct: 6.0
   156|    # FUND_FLOW edges are derived from transactions, not generated.
   157|    fund_flow_min_txn_count: 2
   158|
   159|# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   160|# GAP-06/07 -- typology injection.
   161|# FX conversion alone cannot create Rs 9.4-9.8L clusters against a Rs 10L
   162|# trigger: structuring is INJECTED as a separate, explicitly labelled cohort.
   163|# Bands are expressed as fractions of the CTR threshold resolved from
   164|# GOVERNANCE.POLICY_CLAUSE (CTR_CASH_THRESHOLD), never as literals.
   165|# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   166|injection:
   167|  structuring:
   168|    enabled: true
   169|    cohort_parties: 40
   170|    accounts_per_party_min: 2
   171|    accounts_per_party_max: 4
   172|    deposits_per_account_min: 3
   173|    deposits_per_account_max: 6
   174|    amount_band_pct_of_ctr: [0.90, 0.985]
   175|    window_days: 21
   176|    channel: CASH
   177|    label: reskin_structuring
   178|
   179|  rapid_credit_velocity:
   180|    enabled: true
   181|    cohort_parties: 30
   182|    remitters_min: 7
   183|    remitters_max: 14
   184|    credits_min: 11
   185|    credits_max: 22
   186|    window_days: 3
   187|    label: reskin_mule_fan_in
   188|
   189|  dormant_reactivation:
   190|    enabled: true
   191|    cohort_parties: 20
   192|    dormancy_days_min: 180
   193|    burst_txn_count_min: 8
   194|    label: reskin_dormant_reactivation
   195|
   196|# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   197|# GAP-07 -- realism validation. These are ASSERTED, not claimed. `riskcopilot
   198|# generate` fails if a gate with fail_build: true is violated.
   199|# The AMLworld base rate is 0.063%; subgraph sampling seeded from laundering
   200|# accounts raises it, so the band is stated as a range and enforced.
   201|# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   202|validation:
   203|  illicit_rate_pct:
   204|    min: 0.10
   205|    max: 1.50
   206|    fail_build: true
   207|  money_conservation:
   208|    # Every pair must have exactly one debit leg and one credit leg.
   209|    max_unpaired_legs: 0
   210|    fail_build: true
   211|  referential_integrity:
   212|    max_orphan_account_refs: 0
   213|    max_orphan_party_refs: 0
   214|    fail_build: true
   215|  benford:
   216|    # Chi-square of leading-digit distribution against Benford, legit legs only.
   217|    max_chi_square: 60.0
   218|    fail_build: false          # reported on the realism slide, not a gate
   219|  degree_distribution:
   220|    min_power_law_alpha: 1.5
   221|    max_power_law_alpha: 3.5
   222|    fail_build: false
   223|  label_leakage:
   224|    # V6: no label column may be reachable from the semantic view.
   225|    forbidden_columns: [is_laundering, is_illicit, typology_id, injection_method]
   226|    fail_build: true
   227|  signal_yield:
   228|    # Each Tier-1 rule must produce a non-trivial, non-absurd number of
   229|    # detections, otherwise generation is miscalibrated (this is what catches
   230|    # GAP-04 and GAP-05 regressions automatically).
   231|    min_detections_per_rule: 5
   232|    max_detections_per_rule: 2000
   233|    fail_build: true
   234|
   235|# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   236|# GAP-18 -- the demo hero party must be SELECTED, not assumed. The docs
   237|# hardcode P-10042 / "Rajesh Kumar"; party ids are generated, so the demo
   238|# script would be fiction. This step picks a party that provably trips every
   239|# listed rule and writes the resolved id to conf/generated/demo_entity.yml.
   240|# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   241|demo_entity:
   242|  must_trigger_rules:
   243|    - STRUCTURING_CROSS_ACCOUNT
   244|    - RAPID_CREDIT_VELOCITY
   245|    - SHARED_DEVICE_CLUSTER
   246|  prefer_branch_region: MUMBAI
   247|  prefer_party_type: INDIVIDUAL
   248|  fail_if_not_found: true
   249|
   250|# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   251|# L3 narratives (AI_COMPLETE). Models resolve from conf/models.yml.
   252|# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   253|narratives:
   254|  kyc_notes:
   255|    count: 10000
   256|    temperature: 0.9
   257|    model_key: bulk_narrative
   258|  case_comments:
   259|    count: 2000
   260|    temperature: 0.8
   261|    model_key: bulk_narrative
   262|  golden_documents:
   263|    count: 8
   264|    temperature: 0.3
   265|    model_key: golden_narrative
   266|  # Correlated noise: notes must sometimes CONTRADICT the structured record,
   267|  # so the agent has to reconcile conflicting evidence rather than paraphrase.
   268|  noise:
   269|    typo_pct: 12.0
   270|    contradiction_pct: 8.0
   271|    missing_field_pct: 10.0
   272|    stale_occupation_pct: 6.0
   273|  # One planted prompt injection, for the adversarial suite.
   274|  prompt_injection_count: 3

    41|The 18 diagrams below remain the **design intent**. This section is the **build
    42|truth**, and where the two disagree, this section wins. Diagram-level

    54|| 3 | Load, dynamic tables, streams/tasks, replay harness | Pending |
    55|| 4 | Policy ingestion, Cortex Search, semantic view, agent, 8 procedures | **Blocked** — see §S2 |

    58|Verified: `mypy --strict` clean, `ruff` clean, 105 unit tests passing, all SQL
    59|templates rendering for both profiles, `deploy --stage bootstrap` idempotent

    63|### Repository facts a developer needs
    64|
    65|```
    66|conf/            three-tier config (see below). Nothing hardcoded anywhere.
    67|src/risk_copilot/
    68|  config.py      layered loader, fail-fast validation, sql_context contract
    69|  session.py     connections.toml + key-pair, bootstrap role fallback
    70|  ids.py         deterministic identity derivation (Gap 11 below)

    72|  doctor.py      preflight: config, datasets, connection, capabilities, models
    73|  cli.py         single entry point -- doctor | config | deploy | generate | load | replay | eval
    74|  pipeline/      SQL deployer + offline template lint

    80|**Config is three tiers, and the boundaries are enforced, not conventional:**
    81|
    82|| Tier | What | Where | Enforcement |
    83||---|---|---|---|
    84|| 1 | Credentials | `~/.snowflake/connections.toml`, `cortex secret`, Snowflake `SECRET` | Never in repo; `conf/` holds secret *names* only |
    85|| 2 | Topology (db, schema, warehouse, role, target lag) | `conf/base.yml` + `conf/profiles/{dev,demo}.yml` | `Deployer.render()` **rejects** any `.sql` containing a literal object name |
    86|| 3 | Business thresholds (Rs 10L CTR, 3x income, `COUNT>=3`) | `GOVERNANCE.POLICY_CLAUSE` at runtime, seeded from `conf/detection.yml` | Detection SQL joins `V_POLICY_CLAUSE_CURRENT`; `doctor` fails any clause lacking provenance |

    88|Two profiles coexist in one account: `dev` suffixes every object `_DEV` and

    93|## S2. Account constraints — the dominant planning fact
    94|
    95|**Evidence:** `conf/generated/capabilities.ASHWINRAVI004.yml` — 98 probes,
    96|30 available. That file wins over any prose claim in this repository, including
    97|this section. `riskcopilot doctor` reads it and auto-disables what is absent.
    98|
    99|Account: ZC14131, **STANDARD edition, trial**, AWS_AP_SOUTHEAST_7.
   100|
   101|### Three assumptions that were wrong — do not reintroduce them
   102|
   103|An earlier revision of this section asserted that all Cortex AI was unavailable,
   104|that `SNOWFLAKE.ML` required Enterprise, and that Search/Agent/Analyst were all
   105|blocked because `AI_COMPLETE` was. The probe sweep disproved all three:
   106|
   107|| Claimed | Actual |
   108||---|---|
   109|| All Cortex AI unavailable | **Cortex Analyst works** — NL→SQL over semantic views via REST, HTTP 200, real SQL, served by `claude-sonnet-4-6`. `AI_AGG` and `AI_SUMMARIZE_AGG` work. Text-to-SQL eval (Suite 2) is scorable **now**, not deferred. |
   110|| `SNOWFLAKE.ML` requires Enterprise | **False.** Anomaly detection, Forecast, Model Registry and Feature Store all work on Standard trial. |
   111|| Search/Agent/Analyst blocked because `AI_COMPLETE` is | **Unsound inference.** They are gated independently, and that reasoning is what hid Analyst. Never generalise gating from one probe. |
   112|
   113|### Works — build against these for real
   114|
   115|| Area | Confirmed available |
   116||---|---|
   117|| Critical path | Dynamic tables (+ refresh confirmed), **`STREAM ON DYNAMIC TABLE`**, tasks (warehouse + serverless), `EXECUTE TASK`, `MERGE` with unique constraint, recursive CTE, **Python stored procedures (no Anaconda blocker)**, SQL procedures, Streamlit, network rules |
   118|| Cortex | **Cortex Analyst NL→SQL via REST**, semantic view objects + `SEMANTIC_VIEW()` querying, `AI_AGG`, `AI_SUMMARIZE_AGG`, `CREATE AGENT` (object only), `EXECUTE_AI_EVALUATION` (resolves), threads REST |
   119|| ML | `SNOWFLAKE.ML.ANOMALY_DETECTION`, `FORECAST`, Model Registry, Feature Store |
   120|| Other | `JAROWINKLER_SIMILARITY` / `EDITDISTANCE` / `SOUNDEX`, `CREATE TAG`, email notifications to verified addresses |
   121|
   122|The whole pipeline critical path works. `STREAM ON DYNAMIC TABLE` in particular
   123|was the single biggest unverified dependency — the entire `ROUTE_SIGNALS` design
   124|rests on it.
   125|
   126|### Blocked — trial gate (399258 / 399504 / 509009)
   127|
   128|| Blocked | Diagram | Consequence |
   129||---|---|---|
   130|| **All per-row Cortex inference** — `AI_COMPLETE` (28 models), `SNOWFLAKE.CORTEX.COMPLETE`, 3 REST surfaces. Four independent paths confirmed. | 2 (L3) | Narrative generation. This is now the **only** genuinely blocked piece of the copilot. |
   131|| `AI_CLASSIFY` / `FILTER` / `SENTIMENT` / `EXTRACT` / `PARSE_DOCUMENT` / `TRANSLATE` / `TRANSCRIBE` / `COUNT_TOKENS` / `EMBED` / `SIMILARITY`, plus all legacy equivalents | 3, 10 | Policy ingestion by extraction; KYC-note contradiction detection |
   132|| Cortex Search — `EMBED_TEXT_768/1024` blocked; an explicit `EMBEDDING_MODEL` does not route around it | 3, 10 | `REGULATORY_SEARCH_SVC` |
   133|| Agent **invocation** — 399504 on all 5 paths (SQL ×2, REST ×3). Object creation succeeds. | 7, 13 | Agent-driven orchestration; see §S3 |
   134|| External Access Integration — 509009 | 13 | Kills the Jira / Slack / MCP outbound loop |
   135|
   136|### Blocked — Standard edition (000002 Unsupported feature)
   137|
   138|| Blocked | Diagram | Consequence |
   139||---|---|---|
   140|| Row access policies, masking, tag-based masking, aggregation and projection policies | 11 (G1) | The "same question, two roles, two answers" beat |
   141|| Data Metric Functions | 11 (G6), 12 (Suite 5) | Pipeline-health gates, freshness qualification |
   142|| Time Travel > 1 day | 6, 11 (G3) | `demo.yml`'s `landing_days: 14` **will fail a deploy** |
   143|
   144|### Blocked — regional, not edition or trial
   145|
   146|`SNOWFLAKE.ML.CLASSIFICATION` and `TOP_INSIGHTS` are not served in
   147|AWS_AP_SOUTHEAST_7. **Converting the trial will not fix these** — they need a
   148|different region. `AI_ESTIMATE_QUERY_COST` is parameter-disabled and
   149|`ALTER ACCOUNT` was refused even as ACCOUNTADMIN.

   151|### Genuinely uncertain
   152|
   153|Two findings are inference rather than fact: the 403/003001 → trial
   154|classification (Snowflake's message never says "trial"), and whether
   155|`ENABLE_AI_COST_ESTIMATE` is switchable on this account at all.
   156|
   157|### One design decision that survived the constraint
   158|
   159|Gap 15 below replaced Time-Travel-based re-verification with a materialised
   160|`EVIDENCE_QUERY_LOG.result_snapshot`. Because correctness never depended on

   163|therefore aspirational; the snapshot is the mechanism.

   212|
   213|### Correction to Diagram 7 — two agent modes, not four
   214|
   215|Diagram 7 puts all four roles in one agent. Two of them should never have been
   216|agent modes, and separating them makes the design both more honest and more
   217|buildable today:
   218|
   219|| Role | Correct form | Why |
   220||---|---|---|
   221|| **Reviewer** | **Stored procedure** the orchestrator calls | Its entire value is determinism — numeric recompute against `EVIDENCE_QUERY_LOG`, citation resolution, clause-effective-date checks. Wrapping that in an LLM planner injects nondeterminism into the one component that must not have any. As a procedure it also **works on this account today**, which means the demo's money-shot beat is buildable now. |
   222|| **Sentinel** | SQL view + one `AI_AGG` call | Mostly deterministic ranking plus a summary sentence. An agent turn is slower, costlier and adds nothing. |
   223|| **Investigator** | Agent mode | Genuinely needs multi-step planning and tool selection |
   224|| **Drafter** | Agent mode | Genuinely needs planning; narrative is templated until `AI_COMPLETE` is available |
   225|
   226|General rule: an agent is slower, costlier and nondeterministic. For any fixed
   227|question it is strictly worse than calling Analyst or plain SQL directly, so
   228|**deterministic paths must bypass it entirely.**
   229|
   230|### Why the agent is still a build step
   231|
   232|Cortex Analyst is *one tool* — NL→SQL over one semantic view. It will not call
   233|your stored procedures, will not chain steps, and will not choose between the
   234|semantic view and a graph traversal. That decision layer is the work, and it is
   235|exactly what an agent replaces:
   236|
   237|| Hand-rolled | Agent provides |
   238||---|---|
   239|| Intent routing — which tool answers this? | Tool selection across the registered set |
   240|| The plan loop — query, traverse graph, screen sanctions, re-query | Server-side multi-step planning |
   241|| Conversation state across turns | Threads (REST — confirmed working here) |
   242|| A hosted process to run the loop in | Runs inside Snowflake; a Task can invoke it |
   243|| Tool-call audit logging | Tool-use traces in the response |
   244|| Nothing | RBAC, ownership, lineage (`GET_LINEAGE` supports `CORTEX_AGENT`), MCP exposure, CoWork surface |
   245|
   246|Two consequences matter most here. First, **the three scheduled automations are
   247|only clean via an agent** — a Task can invoke one server-side, whereas a
   248|hand-rolled orchestrator needs a hosted process that, with EAI blocked, cannot
   249|call out anyway. Second, the cross-surface demo beat (CoWork, MCP) comes free
   250|from the object and is otherwise unavailable.
   251|
   252|**The rule that makes the switch cheap: keep tool logic in Snowflake stored
   253|procedures, not in Python.**
   254|
   255|- *Now:* a Python planner calls the 8 procedures + Analyst REST
   256|- *Later:* register the same 8 procedures as agent tools; the agent becomes the
   257|  planner; the Python shrinks to a thin invoke
   258|- *Unchanged either way:* the procedures, semantic view, evidence chain,
   259|  `AGENT_ACTION_LOG`
   260|
   261|If tool logic lives in Python it gets thrown away on migration. That is the
   262|whole reason the 8 tools are stored procedures. `CREATE AGENT` stays a build step
   263|because the object deploys today, it forces tool boundaries to be agent-shaped,
   264|and it lights up unchanged on a non-trial account.
   265|
   266|### Known latent bugs
   267|
   268|1. `conf/profiles/demo.yml` sets `retention.landing_days` / `evidence_days` to
   269|   14. `CREATE SCHEMA` applies these, so **a demo-profile deploy against this
   270|   account will fail.** Cap at 1, or have `config.py` clamp retention using the
   271|   capabilities evidence.
   272|2. `conf/ml.yml:preconditions.require_edition: [ENTERPRISE, BUSINESS_CRITICAL]`
   273|   is contradicted by the probe sweep and **currently disables a working
   274|   feature.** Re-enable `tier1.velocity_anomaly`; move `CLASSIFICATION` and
   275|   `TOP_INSIGHTS` to `future_scope` with "not served in this region" as the
   276|   reason.
   277|
   278|---
   279|
   280|## S4. Diagram corrections
   281|
   282|| Diagram | Stated | Correction |
   283||---|---|---|
   284|| 2 | L2 is an "Agent-Based Simulator"; L3 via `AI_COMPLETE` | L2 is deterministic subgraph sampling + reskin + injection — no simulation. L3 is template-based until Cortex is available. |
   285|| 2 | "5.1K labelled laundering txns" | Actual: 3,209 illicit of 5,078,345 = **0.063%**, which is *below* the stated 0.1% band, not within it. Subgraph sampling raises it; `conf/generation.yml` asserts a 0.10–1.50% band. |
   286|| 3 | Snowpipe Streaming, Marketplace PEP share, live HTTP sanctions fetch | All cut. Replay harness uses batched `INSERT`; sanctions pre-loaded from `data/targets.simple.csv`; the demo has no network dependency. |
   287|| 4 | `DT_TXN_VELOCITY_FEATURES` as a dynamic table with rolling windows | **Not incrementally refreshable.** Decomposed into `DT_TXN_DAILY_AGG` (incremental-safe) + `V_TXN_VELOCITY_FEATURES` (summing view) + `DT_TXN_VELOCITY_1H`. |
   288|| 4 | One `DT_SIGNALS_FAST` holding 5 rules | Split into `DT_SIGNALS_FAST` (row-level, incremental) and `DT_SIGNALS_AGGREGATE` (aggregate/graph, 60 min). One non-incremental rule would degrade the whole table to full refresh every 5 minutes. |
   289|| 4, 15 | `RAW_TRANSACTIONS` shown as the sole landing table | Three tables: `RAW_AMLWORLD_TRANS` (verbatim, pair-level, labelled) → `RAW_TRANSACTIONS` (leg-level, INR, **no label**) + `GROUND_TRUTH.TXN_LABELS`. |
   290|| 5 | Sanctions matching is "exact join only" | Fuzzy matching restored via `JAROWINKLER_SIMILARITY` — one built-in function, not the complexity the original assessment assumed. Exact match raises a signal; the fuzzy band raises a review task. |
   291|| 6, 11 | Evidence "RE-VERIFIABLE via Time Travel" | `EVIDENCE_QUERY_LOG.result_snapshot` + versioned canonical hashing is the mechanism. Time Travel is demonstrable provenance only. |
   292|| 7 | Single Cortex Agent, 4 modes | **Two** agent modes, not four. Reviewer becomes a stored procedure (determinism is its whole value); Sentinel becomes a SQL view + one `AI_AGG` call. Only Investigator and Drafter need planning. Agent *invocation* is trial-gated (399504) but the object deploys — orchestrate from Python over Analyst REST + the procedures meanwhile. See §S3. |
   293|| 8 | "Sanctions name matching scores: exact join" under DETERMINISTIC | Still deterministic, but now `JAROWINKLER_SIMILARITY`. The exact/fuzzy split matters: exact raises a signal, fuzzy raises a review task and may never alone justify a filing. |
   294|| 11 | RLS, masking, DMFs | All Standard-blocked (000002 Unsupported feature). Authored but deploy-gated; equivalent filtering proven via a parameterised view. |
   295|| 12 | 5 test suites | Suite 1 (detection F1) **and Suite 2 (text-to-SQL)** are buildable now — Analyst works, so score on result hash. The deterministic half of Suite 3 (citation resolution) also works. Suite 4 needs `AI_COMPLETE`; Suite 5 needs DMFs. |
   296|| 13 | Jira / Slack / Drive via MCP, agent-as-MCP-server | External Access Integration is trial-gated (509009). Automations run as Snowflake tasks writing to tables; outbound delivery and MCP exposure are out until the account is converted. |
   297|| 14 | Hero party `P-10042 / Rajesh Kumar` | Party ids are **generated**, so this is fiction. A selection step picks a party that provably trips every listed rule and pins it to `conf/generated/demo_entity.yml`. |
   298|| 15 | "16 tables" | Actual count is **28** once staging, ID maps, chunks, templates, proposals, watermark and eval tables are included. |
   299|| 18 | Snowpipe Streaming as future scope | Correct, and now also: replay inserts to `RAW_TRANSACTIONS` directly, and `ingested_at` is distinct from `txn_timestamp` so replay does not corrupt the event clock. |
   300|
   301|---
   302|
   303|## S5. Gaps resolved during implementation
   304|
   305|Gaps 1–10 in the "Fatal Gaps" section below are superseded where they conflict
   306|with this list. Numbering here is independent.
   307|
   308|| # | Problem | Resolution |
   309||---|---|---|
   310|| 1 | Two contradictory `RAW_TRANSACTIONS` definitions (pair-level AMLworld-shaped vs leg-level signed INR), with `is_laundering` in the table that feeds the semantic view | Three-table split (§S4). The label never enters `CURATED`. |
   311|| 2 | **L1 generated Faker parties with fresh ids while transactions referenced AMLworld hex accounts.** Every downstream join would return nothing — no income (kills `INCOME_ACTIVITY_MISMATCH`), no device (kills `SHARED_DEVICE_CLUSTER`), no region (kills RLS). | AMLworld keys are authoritative. `RAW.ID_MAP_PARTY` / `ID_MAP_ACCOUNT` derive surrogate ids deterministically from source keys via `risk_copilot.ids`; Faker only *dresses* preserved keys. Referential integrity holds by construction. |
   312|| 3 | Sampling strategy undefined; 5.08M transactions is unaffordable for a demo | Seed from the 370 laundering attempts' accounts, BFS 2 hops, cut to ~5K entities / ~10K accounts / ~400K legs. A leg is kept only if **both** sides resolve, so `counterparty_account_id` is never an orphan. |
   313|| 4 | `declared_annual_income` assigned at random makes the income rule fire on everyone or nobody | Derived from each party's observed **legitimate** 12-month inflow with a coverage ratio and lognormal noise; the illicit cohort deliberately under-declares at 35%. |
   314|| 5 | `device_fingerprint` at "~8% random" yields **zero** `SHARED_DEVICE_CLUSTER` hits, because the rule needs a shared device **and** a fund flow between the accounts | 70% of shared-device clusters are placed on account groups that already transact; the remaining 30% are decoys the rule must correctly *not* fire on — a built-in false-positive control. |
   315|| 6 | "x83 for INR" across 14 currencies is wrong, and FX conversion cannot create Rs 9.4–9.8L clusters against a Rs 10L trigger | Per-currency rate table; structuring is a **separate labelled injection cohort** with amounts drawn as a fraction of the CTR threshold resolved from `POLICY_CLAUSE`. |
   316|| 7 | Illicit rate claimed "within the 0.1% band" at 0.063% | Band asserted as a build gate (0.10–1.50%), not claimed in prose. |
   317|| 8 | Labels are transaction-grain; signals fire at party/account-window grain. "F1 > 0.7" had no denominator | `GROUND_TRUTH.EVAL_GRAIN_PARTY_MONTH` declares **party-month** as the evaluation grain, carrying `expected_rule_ids` per typology so per-rule recall needs no hand-written mapping. |
   318|| 9 | Patterns file identifies illicit rows only by `(timestamp, from_acct, to_acct, amount)` — not unique — and one pair becomes two legs | Leg-level labels with `match_confidence`; below 1.0 means the source tuple was ambiguous, so uncertainty shows up in the metrics instead of inflating them. |
   319|| 10 | Rolling-window velocity forces full refresh; one non-incremental rule degrades the whole signals table | Velocity decomposed; signals split fast/aggregate (§S4). Channel entropy defined as `-SUM(p*LN(p))` over channel shares — named four times in the original docs, never defined. |
   320|| 11 | **A dynamic table recomputes its full result set every refresh, so the stream + task inserts duplicate `SIGNAL` and `CASE` rows forever.** The original design had no idempotency story. | Deterministic `signal_business_key` = `rule_id\|party_id\|window_bucket[\|account_id]` with a unique constraint; the router `MERGE`s. Keyed on the observation window, not wall-clock time, so it is stable across refreshes. |
   321|| 12 | `SANCTIONS_MATCH_NEW` means "added since last check" — not expressible without persisted state | `RAW.SANCTIONS_SCREENING_WATERMARK`, single-row. |
   322|| 13 | Surrogate ids at 7/8 digits | **Found by test:** 7 digits produced 3 collisions in 5,000 entities and would produce ~24,500 across AMLworld's ~700K — silently merging distinct parties. Widened to 12; a regression test asserts the collision headroom. |
   323|| 14 | RLS covered 2 dynamic tables; cases and findings were unprotected, and owner's-rights procedures **bypass RLS entirely** | `CASE_RECORD.branch_region` denormalised so policies can filter cases. Procedure rights are an explicit decision, not a default. |
   324|| 15 | Reviewer re-verification via Time Travel cannot work: `AT(TIMESTAMP=>)` binds per table reference, retention defaults to 1 day, and dynamic tables are not freely time-travellable. SHA-256 canonicalisation was never defined, so hashes would differ on row order, numeric formatting or null representation. | `EVIDENCE_QUERY_LOG.result_snapshot` + `risk_copilot.hashing`: versioned canonical form, row-order-insensitive, fixed decimal scale, reserved null sentinel, length-prefixed fields. |
   325|| 16 | FIU-IND assumed to publish an XML schema | It publishes a **form**. Our JSON-Schema transcription lives in `REF_FILING_TEMPLATES` with `schema_authority = INTERNAL_TRANSCRIPTION`. No FINGate conformance is claimed. |
   326|| 17 | Demo hero party hardcoded but ids generated | Selection step + pinned config (§S4). |
   327|| 18 | No config layer; thresholds, FX rates, warehouse names and endpoints hardcoded across the docs | Three-tier config with enforcement (§S1). |
   328|| 19 | 30 SQL files, no runner, no ordering, no idempotency | 12 ordered stages, Jinja-templated, `CREATE OR ALTER`/`IF NOT EXISTS` throughout, offline lint, canonical stage ordering regardless of flag order. |
   329|| 20 | ML absent from the design | Tier 1: `JAROWINKLER_SIMILARITY` fuzzy screening (the original docs *cut* this as too complex — it is one built-in function). Future Scope documented with rationale in `conf/ml.yml`. **Hard boundary:** ML may rank and flag for review, never supply a number in an artifact — enforced by `RULE_DEFINITION.admissible_as_primary_evidence`. |
   330|
   331|### Bugs found and fixed in the scaffold itself
   332|
   333|| Fault | Consequence |
   334||---|---|
   335|| `authenticator = externalbrowser` on an account with no SAML configured | Snowflake reports error 390190 naming the "SAML Identity Provider account parameter", which reads as an account fault but is local misconfiguration. Resolved with key-pair (`SNOWFLAKE_JWT`). |
   336|| Role/database/warehouse pinned into the connect string | Rejected with 390189 **before** the tolerant context fallback could run — a chicken-and-egg deadlock making `deploy --stage bootstrap` unreachable. Fallback now drops them only on 390189/390201, never on a credential failure. |
   337|| Statement splitter split on every `;` | A semicolon inside a string literal (`COMMENT = 'Append-only; never updated in place.'`) tore statements in half, failing mid-file after earlier statements had already applied. Replaced with a character scanner respecting quotes, `''` escapes, `--`, `/* */` and `$$`. |
   338|| Adjacent string literals across lines in `COMMENT` clauses | Snowflake does not concatenate them as C does — 60 syntax errors. Fixed and now blocked by a lint rule. |
   339|| `CURRENT_EDITION()` | Not a Snowflake function. Edition now read from `ORGANIZATION_USAGE.ACCOUNTS` with a `SHOW ORGANIZATION ACCOUNTS` fallback. |
   340|| `GRANT ROLE ... TO USER IDENTIFIER(CURRENT_USER())` | Invalid syntax; replaced with dynamic SQL. |

   344|## S6. Build order (solo, thin-slice)
   345|
   346|Build one vertical slice end-to-end before broadening, so a working demo exists
   347|early and everything after it is upside rather than risk.
   348|
   349|1. Generation: subgraph + ID maps + legs + **one** structuring cohort + labels
   350|2. Load
   351|3. Dynamic tables: `dim_party`, `enriched`, `daily_agg`, velocity view, `signals_fast` with **only** `STRUCTURING_CROSS_ACCOUNT`
   352|4. `SIGNALS_STREAM` + `ROUTE_SIGNALS` + `open_case` → a case appears
   353|5. `gather_evidence_bundle` → `EVIDENCE` + `EVIDENCE_QUERY_LOG` with snapshots
   354|6. `generate_str_xml` + `validate_filing_schema` + the **Reviewer procedure**
   355|7. `ATTESTATION` — the human gate
   356|
   357|Step 6 is the demo's money shot (the Reviewer catching a planted defect). Because
   358|the Reviewer is a stored procedure rather than an agent mode (§S3), it needs no
   359|Cortex at all and **runs on this account today**. It belongs in the first slice.
   360|
   361|Then broaden, in demo-value order:
   362|
   363|- remaining 5 signal rules → fuzzy sanctions (`JAROWINKLER_SIMILARITY`)
   364|- semantic view + Cortex Analyst REST → the NL question-answering beat
   365|- Suite 1 (detection F1) and Suite 2 (text-to-SQL, scored on result hash)

   369|- Streamlit

1|# ===========================================================================
     2|# ml.yml -- Snowflake-native ML
     3|# ===========================================================================
     4|# Tier-1 scope is deliberately narrow: the two cheapest high-impact items,
     5|# both of which are BUILT-IN SQL and need no snowflake-ml-python, no compute
     6|# pool, and no model training infrastructure. Everything heavier is recorded
     7|# under future_scope so it can be presented as a considered decision rather
     8|# than an omission.
     9|#
    10|# HARD BOUNDARY, inherited from the LLM boundary rule:
    11|#   ML output may RANK, PRIORITISE and FLAG FOR REVIEW.
    12|#   ML output may never be the sole basis of a filing, and never supplies a
    13|#   number that appears in an artifact. Scores are not evidence.
    14|# ===========================================================================
    15|
    16|enabled: true
    17|
    18|tier1:
    19|
    20|  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    21|  # 1. Fuzzy sanctions screening -- JAROWINKLER_SIMILARITY / EDITDISTANCE.
    22|  #
    23|  # The architecture CUT fuzzy matching as too complex and fell back to exact
    24|  # joins. It is a single built-in scalar function. Restoring it recovers a
    25|  # genuine capability (aliases, transliterations -- the normal case for
    26|  # sanctions screening on Indian names) at near-zero cost.
    27|  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    28|  fuzzy_sanctions:
    29|    enabled: true
    30|    method: JAROWINKLER_SIMILARITY
    31|    # Thresholds resolve from GOVERNANCE.POLICY_CLAUSE
    32|    # (SANCTIONS_EXACT_MATCH, SANCTIONS_FUZZY_REVIEW_FLOOR) -- not from here.
    33|    exact_match_clause_id: SANCTIONS_EXACT_MATCH
    34|    review_floor_clause_id: SANCTIONS_FUZZY_REVIEW_FLOOR
    35|    # Blocking key keeps the cross join tractable against ~500K sanctions rows:
    36|    # candidates must agree on a coarse key before the expensive comparison.
    37|    blocking:
    38|      strategy: soundex_first_token_plus_length_bucket
    39|      max_candidates_per_party: 50
    40|    normalisation:
    41|      uppercase: true
    42|      strip_punctuation: true
    43|      collapse_whitespace: true
    44|      # Dropped before comparison so "Kumar Trading Pvt Ltd" matches "Kumar
    45|      # Trading Private Limited".
    46|      drop_tokens: [LTD, LIMITED, PVT, PRIVATE, LLP, INC, CORP, CO, AND, THE]
    47|    outcome:
    48|      exact: SIGNAL                 # SANCTIONS_MATCH_NEW, severity CRITICAL
    49|      fuzzy: MANUAL_REVIEW          # review task; never an automatic filing
    50|
    51|  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    52|  # 2. Unsupervised velocity anomaly -- SNOWFLAKE.ML.ANOMALY_DETECTION.
    53|  #
    54|  # This is the honest answer to "rule-based TMS produce an 80-95% false
    55|  # positive rate": a per-account behavioural baseline catches deviations that
    56|  # no fixed threshold expresses. Unsupervised, so it does NOT consume
    57|  # GROUND_TRUTH.LABELS and cannot leak them.
    58|  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    59|  velocity_anomaly:
    60|    enabled: true
    61|    function: SNOWFLAKE.ML.ANOMALY_DETECTION
    62|    model_name: RC_VELOCITY_ANOMALY_MODEL
    63|    # Trains on the daily aggregate, which is incremental-safe (GAP-09).
    64|    training_source: DT_TXN_DAILY_AGG
    65|    series_column: account_id
    66|    timestamp_column: txn_date
    67|    target_column: credit_amount_inr
    68|    # Accounts with too little history produce meaningless baselines.
    69|    min_history_days: 45
    70|    prediction_interval: 0.99
    71|    schedule: USING CRON 0 3 * * * Asia/Kolkata
    72|    outcome:
    73|      signal_type: VELOCITY_ANOMALY_ML
    74|      severity: LOW                 # ranks work; never justifies a filing
    75|      # Recorded so the Sentinel can say "flagged by baseline deviation, not by
    76|      # a rule" and the Reviewer can reject any artifact that cites it as
    77|      # primary evidence.
    78|      admissible_as_primary_evidence: false
    79|
    80|# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    81|# Deferred. Each entry states what it would add and why it is not in Tier 1,
    82|# so the "What Production Would Need" slide is specific rather than hand-wavy.
    83|# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    84|future_scope:
    85|
    86|  feature_store:
    87|    package: snowflake.ml.feature_store
    88|    what: >
    89|      Register the velocity features as Feature Views on ACCOUNT and PARTY
    90|      entities, with generate_training_set() for point-in-time-correct
    91|      retrieval.
    92|    why_it_matters: >
    93|      The current design would build any training set by joining current
    94|      feature values to historical labels, which leaks future information and
    95|      inflates measured performance. A Feature Store is the correct fix, not an
    96|      optimisation.
    97|    why_deferred: Not needed while no supervised model is trained in Tier 1.
    98|
    99|  triage_classifier:
   100|    package: SNOWFLAKE.ML.CLASSIFICATION
   101|    what: >
   102|      Supervised risk score trained on GROUND_TRUTH.LABELS with velocity and
   103|      graph features, used ONLY to order the Sentinel's queue.
   104|    why_it_matters: Directly attacks analyst time-to-first-true-positive.
   105|    why_deferred: >
   106|      Requires the Feature Store for point-in-time correctness first;
   107|      otherwise the reported lift is an artefact of leakage. Also needs a
   108|      strict train/test split by TIME, not at random, because the graph makes
   109|      random splits leak.
   110|    guardrail: Ranking only. Never enters EVIDENCE, FINDING or ARTIFACT.
   111|
   112|  top_insights:
   113|    package: SNOWFLAKE.ML.TOP_INSIGHTS
   114|    what: Explain which attributes drive week-over-week alert-volume shifts.
   115|    why_it_matters: Turns the Sentinel summary from a list into an explanation.
   116|    why_deferred: Needs several weeks of simulated history to be meaningful.
   117|
   118|  model_registry:

   275|@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
   276|class FeatureStatus:
   277|    """Evaluation of one feature, with the evidence that decided it."""
   278|
   279|    name: str
   280|    state: FeatureState
   281|    description: str
   282|    fallback: str
   283|    #: Probe ids that are unavailable, each with its failure class and code.
   284|    blockers: tuple[BlockerDetail, ...] = ()
   285|    #: Probe ids the capabilities file says nothing about.
   286|    untested: tuple[str, ...] = ()
   287|
   288|    @property
   289|    def enabled(self) -> bool:
   290|        return self.state is FeatureState.ENABLED
   291|
   292|    def summary(self) -> str:
   293|        """One line explaining the state, naming causes rather than implying them."""
   294|        if self.state is FeatureState.ENABLED:
   295|            return "available"
   296|        if self.state is FeatureState.UNKNOWN:
   297|            missing = ", ".join(self.untested[:4]) or "no capability evidence"
   298|            return f"not established ({missing})"
   299|        causes = "; ".join(
   300|            f"{b.probe_id} [{b.failure_class or 'unclassified'}"
   301|            + (f" {b.error_code}" if b.error_code else "")
   302|            + "]"
   303|            for b in self.blockers[:4]
   304|        )
   305|        return f"blocked by {causes}" if causes else "blocked"
   306|

   308|@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
   309|class BlockerDetail:
   310|    probe_id: str
   311|    failure_class: str | None
   312|    error_code: str | None
   313|
   314|
   315|@dataclass(slots=True)
   316|class Capabilities:
   317|    """The probe results for one connection."""
   318|
   319|    connection: str
   320|    probed_at: str
   321|    account: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
   322|    probes: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = field(default_factory=dict)
   323|    source: Path | None = None
   324|
   325|    @property
   326|    def edition(self) -> str | None:
   327|        value = self.account.get("edition")
   328|        return str(value) if value else None
   329|
   330|    def available(self, probe_id: str) -> bool | None:
   331|        """Return availability, or ``None`` when the probe was never run.
   332|
   333|        The tri-state matters: ``None`` means no evidence, and this module
   334|        deliberately refuses to read that as either yes or no.
   335|        """
   336|        entry = self.probes.get(probe_id)
   337|        if entry is None:
   338|            return None
   339|        return bool(entry.get("available"))
   340|
   341|    def _blocker(self, probe_id: str) -> BlockerDetail:
   342|        entry = self.probes.get(probe_id) or {}
   343|        code = entry.get("error_code")
   344|        return BlockerDetail(
   345|            probe_id=probe_id,
   346|            failure_class=entry.get("failure_class"),
   347|            error_code=str(code) if code is not None else None,
   348|        )
   349|
   350|    def evaluate(self, name: str, feature: Feature) -> FeatureStatus:
   351|        """Decide whether ``feature`` can be built, given the evidence."""
   352|        blockers: list[BlockerDetail] = []
   353|        untested: list[str] = []
   354|
   355|        for probe_id in feature.requires_all:
   356|            outcome = self.available(probe_id)
   357|            if outcome is None:
   358|                untested.append(probe_id)
   359|            elif not outcome:
   360|                blockers.append(self._blocker(probe_id))
   361|
   362|        if feature.requires_any:
   363|            outcomes = {pid: self.available(pid) for pid in feature.requires_any}
   364|            if not any(outcomes.values()):
   365|                if all(v is None for v in outcomes.values()):
   366|                    untested.extend(feature.requires_any)
   367|                else:
   368|                    blockers.extend(self._blocker(pid) for pid, v in outcomes.items() if v is False)
   369|
   370|        if blockers:
   371|            state = FeatureState.DISABLED
   372|        elif untested:
   373|            # Untested is not available. Building on it is exactly the assumption
   374|            # this module exists to stop.
   375|            state = FeatureState.UNKNOWN
   376|        else:
   377|            state = FeatureState.ENABLED
   378|
   379|        return FeatureStatus(
   380|            name=name,
   381|            state=state,
   382|            description=feature.description,
   383|            fallback=feature.fallback,
   384|            blockers=tuple(blockers),
   385|            untested=tuple(dict.fromkeys(untested)),
   386|        )
   387|
   388|    def evaluate_all(self) -> dict[str, FeatureStatus]:
   389|        """Evaluate every feature in :data:`FEATURES`, in declaration order."""
   390|        return {name: self.evaluate(name, spec) for name, spec in FEATURES.items()}
   391|

   393|def capabilities_path(settings: Settings) -> Path:
   394|    """Where the probe writes evidence for the active connection."""
   395|    return (
   396|        settings.repo_root / "conf" / "generated" / f"capabilities.{settings.connection_name}.yml"
   397|    )
   398|
   399|
   400|def load_capabilities(settings: Settings) -> Capabilities | None:
   401|    """Read the capabilities file for the active connection, or ``None``.
   402|
   403|    A missing file is not an error: the probe is a separate, deliberate step, and
   404|    offline work does not need it. The caller reports the absence.
   405|    """
   406|    path = capabilities_path(settings)
   407|    if not path.is_file():
   408|        return None
   409|
   410|    try:
   411|        payload = yaml.safe_load(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) or {}
   412|    except (OSError, yaml.YAMLError):
   413|        logger.debug("Could not read %s", path, exc_info=True)
   414|        return None
   415|
   416|    if not isinstance(payload, dict):
   417|        return None
   418|
   419|    probes = payload.get("probes")
   420|    account = payload.get("account")
   421|    return Capabilities(
   422|        connection=str(payload.get("connection", settings.connection_name)),
   423|        probed_at=str(payload.get("probed_at", "unknown")),
   424|        account=account if isinstance(account, dict) else {},
   425|        probes=probes if isinstance(probes, dict) else {},
   426|        source=path,
   427|    )
   428|
   429|
   430|def on_unavailable_policy(settings: Settings) -> str:
   431|    """Return the configured policy for an unmet precondition.
   432|
   433|    Defaults to ``disable_and_report``: a hard failure at demo time is the worst
   434|    available outcome, so it is never the default.
   435|    """
   436|    preconditions = (settings.ml.get("preconditions") or {}) if settings.ml else {}
   437|    value = str(preconditions.get("on_unavailable") or DISABLE_AND_REPORT).strip().lower()
   438|    return value if value in (DISABLE_AND_REPORT, FAIL) else DISABLE_AND_REPORT

1|"""Layered configuration loader.

     4|
     5|    conf/base.yml                     topology defaults
     6|    conf/profiles/<profile>.yml       environment overlay (deep-merged)
     7|    conf/<domain>.yml                 generation / detection / models / external / ml
     8|    <domain>_overrides in the profile  profile-specific domain tweaks
     9|    environment variables (RC_*)      developer escape hatch
    10|    explicit CLI flags                highest precedence
    11|
    12|Two rules make this worth having rather than decoration:
    13|
    14|1. **Nothing is hardcoded.** No database, schema, warehouse, role or threshold
    15|   literal appears in Python or SQL. SQL files are Jinja templates rendered
    16|   with :meth:`Settings.sql_context`.
    17|2. **Business thresholds are not config at runtime.** ``conf/detection.yml`` is
    18|   a *seed* for ``GOVERNANCE.POLICY_CLAUSE``; detection SQL joins to that table.
    19|   This module loads the seed so it can be deployed and validated, and
    20|   deliberately offers no API for reading a threshold at detection time.
    21|"""

    23|from __future__ import annotations
    24|
    25|import copy
    26|import os

    29|from pathlib import Path
    30|from typing import Any

    43|#: Snowflake unquoted identifiers: letter/underscore start, then alphanumerics

    61|class ConfigError(RuntimeError):
    62|    """Raised when configuration is missing, malformed or internally inconsistent.
    63|
    64|    Always raised eagerly at load time. A misconfigured deploy must fail before
    65|    it touches Snowflake, not halfway through creating objects.

    74|def deep_merge(base: dict[str, Any], overlay: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    75|    """Recursively merge ``overlay`` over ``base``, returning a new dict.
    76|
    77|    Dicts merge key-wise; every other type (including lists) is replaced
    78|    wholesale. Replacing lists is deliberate -- a profile that narrows
    79|    ``branch_regions`` must be able to shorten the list, not append to it.
    80|    """
    81|    result = copy.deepcopy(base)
    82|    for key, value in overlay.items():
    83|        existing = result.get(key)
    84|        if isinstance(existing, dict) and isinstance(value, dict):
    85|            result[key] = deep_merge(existing, value)
    86|        else:
    87|            result[key] = copy.deepcopy(value)
    88|    return result

    91|def _read_yaml(path: Path) -> dict[str, Any]:

    94|    try:
    95|        loaded = yaml.safe_load(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    96|    except yaml.YAMLError as exc:  # pragma: no cover - surfaced verbatim
    97|        raise ConfigError(f"Malformed YAML in {path}: {exc}") from exc
    98|    if loaded is None:
    99|        return {}
   100|    if not isinstance(loaded, dict):
   101|        raise ConfigError(f"Expected a mapping at the top level of {path}")

   105|def validate_identifier(value: str, *, what: str) -> str:
   106|    """Return ``value`` upper-cased, or raise if it is not a safe identifier.

   108|    Guards the DDL-rendering path: these strings are interpolated into SQL, so
   109|    an unvalidated value from a YAML file would be an injection point.

   111|    if not isinstance(value, str) or not _IDENTIFIER_RE.match(value):
   112|        raise ConfigError(
   113|            f"{what} must be a valid unquoted Snowflake identifier "
   114|            f"(letters, digits, underscore; not starting with a digit), got {value!r}"

   281|class Settings(BaseModel):
   282|    """Fully resolved, immutable configuration for one profile.
   283|
   284|    Build with :meth:`load`. Direct construction is supported for tests but
   285|    bypasses the layering.
   286|    """
   287|
   288|    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True, extra="forbid", arbitrary_types_allowed=True)
   289|
   290|    repo_root: Path
   291|    profile: str
   292|    object_suffix: str
   293|
   294|    database: str
   295|    schemas: Schemas
   296|    warehouses: dict[str, Warehouse]
   297|    roles: Roles

   300|    dynamic_tables: dict[str, DynamicTableSpec]

   304|
   305|    # Domain configs are kept as plain mappings: they are large, mostly
   306|    # data-shaped, and consumed by the generators that own their semantics.
   307|    # Validating them here would duplicate that ownership.
   308|    generation: dict[str, Any] = Field(default_factory=dict)
   309|    detection: dict[str, Any] = Field(default_factory=dict)
   310|    models: dict[str, Any] = Field(default_factory=dict)

   314|    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
   315|    # Cross-section consistency
   316|    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
   317|
   318|    @model_validator(mode="after")
   319|    def _check_consistency(self) -> Settings:
   320|        for required in ("dev", "pipeline", "demo"):
   321|            if required not in self.warehouses:
   322|                raise ConfigError(f"Missing required warehouse definition: {required!r}")
   323|
   324|        # A branch analyst role whose region is never generated silently makes
   325|        # the RLS demo return an empty result instead of a filtered one -- a
   326|        # failure that looks like working access control.
   327|        configured = set(self.roles.branch_analysts)
   328|        generated = {
   329|            str(entry["code"]).upper()
   330|            for entry in self.generation.get("entities", {}).get("branch_regions", [])
   331|            if isinstance(entry, dict) and "code" in entry
   332|        }
   333|        if generated and not configured <= generated:
   334|            missing = sorted(configured - generated)
   335|            raise ConfigError(
   336|                f"Branch analyst roles exist for regions that generation never "
   337|                f"produces: {missing}. The row-access-policy demo would show an "
   338|                f"empty result rather than a filtered one. Reconcile "
   339|                f"conf/base.yml:roles.branch_analysts with "
   340|                f"conf/generation.yml:entities.branch_regions."
   341|            )
   342|
   343|        # Severity keys must be known, or ROUTE_SIGNALS cannot rank.
   344|        order = {s.upper() for s in self.detection.get("routing", {}).get("severity_order", [])}
   345|        if order:
   346|            unknown = {
   347|                sev.upper()
   348|                for sev in self.detection.get("severity", {}).values()
   349|                if sev.upper() not in order
   350|            }
   351|            if unknown:
   352|                raise ConfigError(
   353|                    f"conf/detection.yml assigns severities not present in "
   354|                    f"routing.severity_order: {sorted(unknown)}"
   355|                )

   359|    # Loading
   360|    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
   361|
   362|    @classmethod
   363|    def load(
   364|        cls,
   365|        repo_root: Path | str | None = None,
   366|        profile: str | None = None,
   367|        *,
   368|        overrides: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
   369|    ) -> Settings:
   370|        """Resolve configuration for ``profile``.
   371|
   372|        Args:
   373|            repo_root: Repository root. Defaults to the package's grandparent.
   374|            profile: ``dev`` or ``demo``. Falls back to ``RC_PROFILE``, then
   375|                :data:`DEFAULT_PROFILE`.
   376|            overrides: Highest-precedence topology overrides, deep-merged last.
   377|                Intended for CLI flags and tests.
   378|

   380|            ConfigError: If a file is missing, malformed, or the resolved
   381|                configuration is internally inconsistent.
   382|        """

   384|        conf_dir = root / "conf"
   385|
   386|        resolved_profile = (profile or _env_override("PROFILE") or DEFAULT_PROFILE).lower()
   387|        if resolved_profile not in VALID_PROFILES:
   388|            raise ConfigError(
   389|                f"Unknown profile {resolved_profile!r}; expected one of {list(VALID_PROFILES)}"
   390|            )
   391|
   392|        merged = _read_yaml(conf_dir / "base.yml")
   393|        merged = deep_merge(merged, _read_yaml(conf_dir / "profiles" / f"{resolved_profile}.yml"))
   394|
   395|        domains = {key: _read_yaml(conf_dir / name) for key, name in _DOMAIN_FILES.items()}
   396|
   397|        # `<domain>_overrides` in a profile tweaks a domain config without
   398|        # duplicating it. Keeps dev.yml to a readable diff.
   399|        for domain in domains:
   400|            overlay = merged.pop(f"{domain}_overrides", None)
   401|            if overlay:
   402|                if not isinstance(overlay, dict):
   403|                    raise ConfigError(
   404|                        f"{resolved_profile}.yml: {domain}_overrides must be a mapping"
   405|                    )
   406|                domains[domain] = deep_merge(domains[domain], overlay)
   407|
   408|        if overrides:
   409|            merged = deep_merge(merged, overrides)
   410|
   411|        # --- environment escape hatches ---------------------------------- #
   412|        database = _env_override("DATABASE") or merged["database"]["name"]
   413|        suffix = merged.get("project", {}).get("object_suffix", "") or ""
   414|
   415|        warehouses = {
   416|            key: Warehouse(**spec) for key, spec in (merged.get("warehouses") or {}).items()
   417|        }
   418|        if wh := _env_override("WAREHOUSE"):
   419|            # Point every role at one warehouse -- used when developing against
   420|            # a warehouse you did not create.
   421|            forced = validate_identifier(wh, what="RC_WAREHOUSE")
   422|            warehouses = {k: v.model_copy(update={"name": forced}) for k, v in warehouses.items()}
   423|
   424|        roles_raw = dict(merged.get("roles") or {})
   425|        if role := _env_override("ROLE"):
   426|            roles_raw["admin"] = role
   427|
   428|        if seed := _env_override("SEED"):
   429|            try:
   430|                domains["generation"]["seed"] = int(seed)
   431|            except ValueError as exc:
   432|                raise ConfigError(f"RC_SEED must be an integer, got {seed!r}") from exc
   433|
   434|        if conn := _env_override("SNOWFLAKE_CONNECTION"):
   435|            domains["external"].setdefault("snowflake", {})["connection_name"] = conn
   436|
   437|        try:
   438|            return cls(
   439|                repo_root=root,
   440|                profile=resolved_profile,
   441|                object_suffix=suffix,
   442|                database=validate_identifier(database, what="Database name"),
   443|                schemas=Schemas(**merged["schemas"]),
   444|                warehouses=warehouses,
   445|                roles=Roles(**roles_raw),
   446|                stages=Stages(**merged["stages"]),
   447|                retention=Retention(**merged["retention"]),
   448|                dynamic_tables={
   449|                    key: DynamicTableSpec(**spec)
   450|                    for key, spec in (merged.get("dynamic_tables") or {}).items()
   451|                },
   452|                views={
   453|                    k: validate_identifier(v, what="View name")
   454|                    for k, v in (merged.get("views") or {}).items()
   455|                },
   456|                streams_tasks=dict(merged.get("streams_tasks") or {}),
   457|                cortex=CortexObjects(**merged["cortex"]),
   458|                generation=domains["generation"],
   459|                detection=domains["detection"],
   460|                models=domains["models"],
   461|                external=domains["external"],
   462|                ml=domains["ml"],
   463|            )
   464|        except KeyError as exc:
   465|            raise ConfigError(f"Missing required configuration section: {exc}") from exc

   467|    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
   468|    # Name resolution
   469|    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
   470|
   471|    def obj(self, name: str) -> str:
   472|        """Apply the profile's object suffix to a bare object name.
   473|
   474|        Keeps a ``dev`` deploy from colliding with ``demo`` objects in the same
   475|        account.
   476|        """
   477|        return f"{name.upper()}{self.object_suffix.upper()}"

   482|
   483|    def fq(self, schema_key: str, name: str | None = None) -> str:

   485|
   486|        Args:

   488|                rather than a literal schema name, so a schema rename is a
   489|                one-line config change.

   493|            schema = getattr(self.schemas, schema_key)
   494|        except AttributeError as exc:

   496|                f"Unknown schema key {schema_key!r}; expected one of {list(Schemas.model_fields)}"
   497|            ) from exc

   515|                f"Unknown warehouse key {key!r}; expected one of {sorted(self.warehouses)}"

   525|                "conf/external.yml:snowflake.connection_name or RC_SNOWFLAKE_CONNECTION."

   529|    def model_for(self, role: str) -> list[str]:

   531|
   532|        A *list* is returned on purpose: model availability is region-dependent,
   533|        so the caller picks the first name the doctor confirmed rather than

1|"""``riskcopilot`` -- the single entry point for every operation.
     2|
     3|No part of this project is invoked by running a loose script: every operation
     4|is a subcommand, so the profile, logging and configuration resolution are
     5|identical no matter who runs it.

    54|def _load_dotenv(start: Path | None = None) -> Path | None:
    55|    """Load ``.env`` into the environment, returning the file used.
    56|
    57|    ``.env`` holds pointers -- which connection to use, where the private key
    58|    lives -- and every consumer reads them via :mod:`os.environ`. Loading it
    59|    here means one entry point applies it, so a developer does not have to
    60|    export the same variables by hand in every shell. Values already present in
    61|    the environment win, so an explicit ``RC_*`` override on the command line is
    62|    never clobbered by the file. Parsed with the standard library rather than
    63|    adding a dependency for eight lines of work.
    64|    """
    65|    origin = (start or Path.cwd()).resolve()
    66|    for directory in (origin, *origin.parents):
    67|        candidate = directory / ".env"
    68|        if candidate.is_file():
    69|            break
    70|    else:
    71|        return None
    72|
    73|    for raw in candidate.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
    74|        line = raw.strip()
    75|        if not line or line.startswith("#") or "=" not in line:
    76|            continue
    77|        key, _, value = line.partition("=")
    78|        key = key.strip()
    79|        value = value.strip().strip('"').strip("'")
    80|        if key and key not in os.environ:
    81|            os.environ[key] = value
    82|    return candidate

1|"""Deterministic identity derivation -- the referential backbone.
     2|
     3|This module exists because of GAP-02, the most serious defect in the original
     4|plan. The architecture generated ~5K Faker parties with fresh ids while the
     5|transaction ledger referenced IBM AMLworld's hex account ids. Nothing
     6|reconciled the two, so every downstream join would have silently returned
     7|nothing: no declared income (killing INCOME_ACTIVITY_MISMATCH), no device
     8|fingerprint (killing SHARED_DEVICE_CLUSTER), no branch region (killing the
     9|row-access-policy demo).
    10|
    11|The fix is to invert the direction of generation. AMLworld's keys are
    12|authoritative; L1 *enriches* them rather than replacing them. Every synthetic
    13|attribute is derived from a stable hash of the source key, which buys three
    14|properties:
    15|
    16|* **Referential integrity by construction.** A party id is a pure function of
    17|  an AMLworld ``entity_id``, so a transaction leg can never reference a party
    18|  that generation did not produce.
    19|* **Idempotence.** Re-running generation, or resampling at a different size,
    20|  yields the same id and the same attributes for the same source entity.
    21|* **Reproducible-but-uncorrelated attributes.** Each attribute draws from its
    22|  own derived stream, so risk rating and branch region are independent even
    23|  though both descend from one seed.
    24|"""
    25|
    26|from __future__ import annotations
    27|
    28|import hashlib
    29|import random
    30|import re
    31|from collections.abc import Sequence
    32|from typing import TypeVar
    33|
    34|T = TypeVar("T")
    35|
    36|#: Zero-padding widths.
    37|#:
    38|#: Sized against the FULL AMLworld population (~700K entities, 518,581
    39|#: accounts), not the sampled subgraph, so an id stays stable if the sample
    40|#: grows. Width is a collision-probability decision, not a cosmetic one: a
    41|#: collision merges two distinct entities and silently corrupts the counterparty
    42|#: graph, which is precisely the class of failure this module exists to prevent.
    43|#:
    44|#: With n keys drawn uniformly over m values, expected collisions ~= n^2 / 2m.
    45|#: At n = 700,000:
    46|#:     width  7 (m = 1e7)  -> ~24,500 collisions   unusable
    47|#:     width 10 (m = 1e10) -> ~24 collisions       still unacceptable
    48|#:     width 12 (m = 1e12) -> ~0.25 collisions     acceptable
    49|#: Twelve digits is therefore the floor. Generation additionally asserts that the
    50|#: emitted map is 1:1 and fails loudly rather than merging, so a rare collision
    51|#: is a build failure rather than silent corruption.
    52|PARTY_ID_WIDTH = 12
    53|ACCOUNT_ID_WIDTH = 12
    54|TXN_ID_WIDTH = 12
    55|
    56|PARTY_ID_PREFIX = "P-"
    57|ACCOUNT_ID_PREFIX = "A-"
    58|TXN_ID_PREFIX = "T-"
    59|PAIR_ID_PREFIX = "TP-"
    60|
    61|_PARTY_ID_RE = re.compile(rf"^{PARTY_ID_PREFIX}\d{{{PARTY_ID_WIDTH}}}$")
    62|_ACCOUNT_ID_RE = re.compile(rf"^{ACCOUNT_ID_PREFIX}\d{{{ACCOUNT_ID_WIDTH}}}$")
    63|
    64|#: Modulus for surrogate ids. 10**width, so the formatted id never overflows
    65|#: its declared width. Collisions are possible in principle at these widths;
    66|#: the generator asserts uniqueness of the emitted map and fails loudly rather
    67|#: than silently merging two entities.
    68|_PARTY_MOD = 10**PARTY_ID_WIDTH
    69|_ACCOUNT_MOD = 10**ACCOUNT_ID_WIDTH
    70|
    71|
    72|def stable_hash(*parts: object, namespace: str = "") -> int:
    73|    """Return a stable 64-bit integer digest of ``parts``.
    74|
    75|    Uses BLAKE2b rather than :func:`hash`, whose output is salted per process
    76|    and therefore useless for reproducibility.
    77|
    78|    Args:
    79|        *parts: Values joined with ``\\x1f`` (unit separator, which cannot occur
    80|            in the source keys) so that ``("a", "bc")`` and ``("ab", "c")``
    81|            digest differently.
    82|        namespace: Domain separator. Distinct namespaces give uncorrelated
    83|            streams from the same inputs, which is what keeps derived
    84|            attributes independent.
    85|    """
    86|    payload = "\x1f".join(str(p) for p in (namespace, *parts))
    87|    return int.from_bytes(hashlib.blake2b(payload.encode("utf-8"), digest_size=8).digest(), "big")
    88|
    89|
    90|def derived_rng(*parts: object, seed: int, namespace: str = "") -> random.Random:
    91|    """Return a :class:`random.Random` seeded deterministically from ``parts``.
    92|
    93|    The per-entity generator pattern. Rather than drawing every attribute from
    94|    one global stream -- where output depends on iteration order -- each entity
    95|    gets its own stream keyed by its identity. Attributes are then stable
    96|    regardless of how many entities are generated or in what order.
    97|    """
    98|    return random.Random(stable_hash(seed, *parts, namespace=namespace))  # noqa: S311

   102|# Surrogate identifiers
   103|# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
   104|
   105|
   106|def party_id(entity_id: str, *, seed: int) -> str:
   107|    """Derive a stable ``P-#######`` id from an AMLworld ``entity_id``.
   108|
   109|    Args:
   110|        entity_id: Hex entity id from ``HI-Small_accounts.csv``.
   111|        seed: Master generation seed.
   112|    """
   113|    if not entity_id or not str(entity_id).strip():
   114|        raise ValueError("entity_id must be a non-empty string")
   115|    n = stable_hash(str(entity_id).strip().upper(), seed, namespace="party") % _PARTY_MOD
   116|    return f"{PARTY_ID_PREFIX}{n:0{PARTY_ID_WIDTH}d}"
   117|
   118|
   119|def account_id(bank_id: str, account_number: str, *, seed: int) -> str:
   120|    """Derive a stable ``A-########`` id from AMLworld's composite account key.
   121|
   122|    AMLworld account numbers are unique only within a bank, so the surrogate
   123|    must derive from ``(bank_id, account_number)``. Deriving from the account
   124|    number alone would merge distinct accounts across banks -- silently
   125|    corrupting the counterparty graph.
   126|    """
   127|    if not account_number or not str(account_number).strip():
   128|        raise ValueError("account_number must be a non-empty string")
   129|    n = (
   130|        stable_hash(
   131|            str(bank_id).strip().upper(),
   132|            str(account_number).strip().upper(),
   133|            seed,
   134|            namespace="account",
   135|        )
   136|        % _ACCOUNT_MOD
   137|    )
   138|    return f"{ACCOUNT_ID_PREFIX}{n:0{ACCOUNT_ID_WIDTH}d}"
   139|

   141|def txn_pair_id(sequence: int) -> str:
   142|    """Return the shared id linking a debit leg to its credit leg (GAP-03).
   143|
   144|    One AMLworld row becomes two legs. They share this id, which is what
   145|    ``V_TRANSACTION_PAIRS`` self-joins on to recover the pair-level shape that
   146|    graph queries need.
   147|    """
   148|    if sequence < 0:
   149|        raise ValueError("sequence must be non-negative")
   150|    return f"{PAIR_ID_PREFIX}{sequence:0{TXN_ID_WIDTH}d}"
   151|
   152|
   153|def txn_leg_id(pair_id: str, side: str) -> str:
   154|    """Return the leg-level transaction id for one side of a pair.
   155|
   156|    Args:
   157|        pair_id: Value from :func:`txn_pair_id`.
   158|        side: ``"D"`` (debit) or ``"C"`` (credit).
   159|    """
   160|    normalised = side.strip().upper()
   161|    if normalised not in {"D", "C"}:
   162|        raise ValueError(f"side must be 'D' or 'C', got {side!r}")
   163|    return f"{TXN_ID_PREFIX}{pair_id.removeprefix(PAIR_ID_PREFIX)}-{normalised}"
   164|

   166|def is_party_id(value: str) -> bool:
